notes:
Topline: Large regional trust bank evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for sensitive document search, chat assistant for client operations, and transaction-level reranking. Primary ask: run full POC inside their AWS account (VPC) with Terraform + Helm deliverables, KMS integration and audit log shipping to their SIEM. Short, messy notes below — from AE/SE/Legal threads and call transcripts.

- Opportunity origin: warm intro from channel partner (banking-specialist SI). Initial demo 2026-01-20, technical follow-up 2026-02-12 (FF call).
- Quote from CTO (2026-02-12): "We need provable separation of keys and logs — can't have tokens or PII leaving our tenancy." They repeated data residency must be US-only for this workload.
- Deployment ask: POC deployed via our Terraform modules into customer VPC, helm charts to k8s EKS cluster. Deliverables: terraform plan, helm values, IAM policy docs, test harness for end-to-end inference (latency + correctness).
- Security: must integrate with customer AWS KMS CMKs. SE note: we need one-time KMS key policy edits and an STS role for instance profile. Legal is asking for DPA + security questionnaire; SOC2 report requested.
- Observability: logs to be forwarded to customer SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) via Fluentd. Audit trail requirements include request/response hashes (no raw PII), keystamped events, and integration with their audit-logging pipeline.
- Traffic/routing: strict egress rules — only outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints over signed mTLS from a dedicated nat gateway; they want explicit IP allowlist.
- Performance targets: 95th percentile latency < 150 ms for short-chat (<=128 tokens), sustained throughput 200 req/s for batch reranking jobs. Cost sensitivity: moderate — prefer batching/quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
- POC success criteria (from SE/AE alignment): 1) Terraform + Helm applied without infra changes outside agreed subnets; 2) KMS CMK encryption for model cache and logs; 3) audit logs visible in SIEM with trace ids mapped back to requests; 4) SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning works for demo users; 5) formal security sign-off from InfoSec.
- Customer infra contacts: infra-eng@argus-trust.com (primary), secops lead: Jenna Alvarez. Procurement contact: David Moreno.
- AE/SE chitchat: need to scope run hours for Dedicated fallback during POC (warm pool for model weights) — cost + network egress questions.
- Risks: KMS policy edits may require crypto team approval (2-week lead), procurement SOW timeline uncertain, firewall team slow to open CIDR range for control-plane connectivity.
- Next: send POC runbook v2 (drive link), get list of NAT/public egress IPs from Argus infra, schedule infra/SEC workshop week of 2026-03-08.
- Short-term ask from customer: "Can you provide a step-by-step Terraform plan and an offline validation checklist?" (from Jenna A.)

requirements_summary: Workload types: chat assistant (low latency), document search (embeddings), reranking (batch)
Latency target: p95 < 150ms for chat (<=128 tokens)
Throughput: 200 req/s sustained for reranking; burst to 1k req/s for short windows
Data residency: US-only; logs and model cache must not leave us-east-1
KMS: customer-managed CMKs; must support envelope encryption for model artifacts and caching; key policy edits allowed with review
Audit logging: forward application + access logs to Splunk, include request trace ids; retention controls per retention policy (7 years for specific events)
IAM: cross-account assume-role for deployment automation; least-privilege terraform plan required
Networking: private subnets, no public IPs on pods, outbound allowlist to Redwood control-plane via NAT; optional VPC endpoints considered
